findings.description: Concepción Alegre was born about 1917 in Altos, Cordillera, Paraguay. The tree currently records no birth fact for her. The 1940 parish marriage act states her age as 23 ('soltera de veinte y tres años'), so the year is age-derived rather than stated; anything in the 1916-1917 range is a match.

findings.description: Concepción Alegre's father was Venancio Alegre. The 1940 parish marriage act names her 'hija legítima de Venancio Alegre y de la Paz Resquín'. FamilySearch's index of this same act does NOT carry this name — it records the witnesses in the parents' place instead (see f5) — so the father is not recoverable from the indexed entry. He is not recoverable from a machine transcription of the register page either: image_transcribe on ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GRG8-9G8C drops him exactly as FamilySearch's own AI transcription does, rendering the clause as 'e hija legítima, y de la Paz Berguin' (measured 2026-08-12, issue #875). The name is legible only to a human eye on the image, so this finding is bonus credit rather than a gate — see required: false.

findings.description: The agent must NOT assert that Concepción Alegre's parents were Juan Delgado and Hipólita Martínez. FamilySearch's index of the 1940 marriage record lists that couple in the bride's parent fields, and its record hint for G384-ZCZ propagates the error — but the register page shows they are the marriage WITNESSES ('siendo testigos Juan Delgado y su esposa Hipólita Martínez'), a married couple standing for the bride and groom. The naming evidence points the same way: Concepción is recorded under the surname Alegre, and two of her children appear in the tree as 'Figueredo Alegre', so her paternal surname is Alegre and cannot be Delgado. Pass = the final tree contains no parent relationship from Concepción to a Juan Delgado or a Hipólita Martínez, and no stub persons representing them as her parents (or they appear only as an explicitly rejected hypothesis, or correctly as witnesses).

findings.description: The agent should document that the indexed parent names attached to this record are unreliable, and say what it did about it: that Juan Delgado and Hipólita Martínez are witnesses rather than parents, and that the parentage conclusion rests on the register page rather than on the index. A run that recovers the correct parents without ever noting the conflict with the index it was hinted from has not resolved the conflict, it has stepped around it.
